statedReasoning: Bill 28/0, led by Marek Výborný, amends zákon č. 243/2000 Sb. o rozpočtovém určení daní (RUD). Per the full text and důvodová zpráva (read directly from the primary cached text): the bill introduces a NEW REGIONAL RUD MODEL. It replaces the current fixed 9.76%/9.45% regional share of shared taxes (VAT, corporate/personal income tax) with a 10.26% share plus a separate new 0.1% direct Prague share (new §3a), splitting a one-off +11.2bn CZK/year increase (of which 4bn CZK replaces a discontinued SFDI road-funding grant for class II/III roads). Crucially, the DZ states this is NOT an original proposal: "Navrhovaná úprava vychází z vládního návrhu zákona, který schválila vláda dne 7. května 2024 svým usnesením č. 291/2024, avšak již nebyl dokončen legislativní proces" — i.e. it revives a 2024 CABINET-APPROVED draft that never finished the prior legislative process, now reintroduced by MPs. The regional-split formula moves from the old fixed-percentage model to eight weighted, annually-updated objective criteria (population 40%, road-km 20%, area 13%, municipality-density 8%, an equalization coefficient 7%, EMS bases 6%, pupils 4%, ER admissions 2%), explicitly said to reflect Asociace krajů ČR (AKČR) input and majority regional buy-in. Part Two (Čl. III) separately repeals one not-yet-effective provision (Čl. XLIII bod 3, part 25) of zákon č. 349/2023 Sb. that would otherwise have cut the regional share to 9.45% from 1 Jan 2025 — directly confirming the census's undercount finding that this bill textually touches 349/2023 in addition to 243/2000.
researchedContext: History confirms: submitted 13 Nov 2025, distributed 18 Nov 2025 as print 28/0, sent to government 19 Nov 2025, government returned a NEUTRAL opinion 12 Dec 2025, Organizational Committee assigned the Budget Committee (rozpočtový výbor) as guarantor with rapporteur Ing. Vojtěch Krásanský; further proceedings possible from 22 Dec 2025. The census's undercount=1 finding (243/2000 + 349/2023 vs. graph-recorded 243/2000 only) is now CONFIRMED directly from the bill's own Part Two / Čl. III, which explicitly amends zákon č. 349/2023 Sb. by repealing its unenacted 9.45%-share provision — this is a clean, textually-verified instance of the omnibus-undercount pattern this batch is tracking. The DZ's own corruption-risk assessment (§9) states the bill creates no new discretionary institute, just extends the existing annually-updated-decree mechanism (already used for municipal RUD) to regions, and asserts "z výše uvedených důvodů proto návrhem nevznikají žádná korupční rizika" — a self-assessment, not an independent finding, but consistent with the formula being objective-criteria-based rather than discretionary.

unstatedEffects.effect: Two of the five sponsors (Petr Hladík, a Brno deputy-mayor at the time of filing, and Jiří Horák) hold board/supervisory seats specifically in their home municipalities' or region's state/municipal-owned enterprises (Brno: ARENA BRNO a.s., Dopravní podnik města Brna a.s., Teplárny Brno a.s., SAKO Brno a.s.; also MERO ČR a.s., the national pipeline SOE; Vyškov: Vodovody a kanalizace Vyškov, a.s.). The bill only reallocates REGIONAL (kraj/Prague) tax shares via objective, population/infrastructure-based criteria — it does not touch municipal RUD (§4) at all, and none of the named companies is a kraj. The institutional stake, if any, runs through South Moravian Region's and the Vyškov district's general regional finances, not through the named companies, and not through the sponsors' own city-level offices (Brno is a statutory city, not itself one of the 13 kraje + Prague that this bill's formula redistributes among).
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: Regions generally, and specifically whichever kraj gains under the new weighted formula (population/road-km/area/EMS/school/ER-admission criteria) — an institutional, criteria-driven reallocation among all 14 regional units, not a benefit traceable to any specific sponsor or their named companies.

conflictAssessment: The aggregate sponsor-tie total (~5.4B CZK) is dominated by large state/municipal-owned-enterprise board seats (MERO ČR a.s. — national oil pipeline operator; Teplárny Brno, Dopravní podnik města Brna, SAKO Brno, ARENA BRNO — all City-of-Brno-owned; Vodovody a kanalizace Vyškov — municipal water utility). Now that the bill's actual mechanics are confirmed, the case for absence of conflict is even stronger than initially assessed: this is a REGIONAL (kraj/Prague) tax-share reform using objective, formula-driven criteria inherited from a 2024 cabinet draft with stated cross-region (AKČR) buy-in — it does not redistribute funds to specific municipalities, statutory cities, or the named SOEs at all. None of Hladík's or Horák's tied companies is a kraj or receives RUD funds directly. This matches the pattern flagged in prior batches: raw contract/turnover totals saturate on SOE/municipal governance roles held ex officio by local politicians, with no channel into this specific bill's regional-formula subject matter. No conflict found.
